title: Build a dynamic science lesson: density, quantities and a constant-density model

audience.curriculum: England; illustrative secondary study, not a confirmed school assignment
audience.level: Ages 12–14 starting example; school year and exam scope must be configured

objectives.description: Calculate density from exact mass and volume in the declared units; distinguish the idealised model from measurement.

contentRequirements: Explain density and the mass/volume relationship with cited worked examples and labelled units.
Describe the idealised constant-density model, constructed data and all excluded phenomena; do not name real substances.
Define two binary criteria density-value and density-unit, one mark each, including unsupported-unit handling.
Explain why varying volume at fixed density changes mass; this explanation does not itself establish student causal understanding.

generation.algorithm: Use a declared seeded PRNG to choose a valid (d,v); calculate m exactly. Freeze prompt, parameters and two-criterion rubric.
constraints: Exactly 80 possible parameter pairs; all v are positive.
Only density-from-mass-and-volume questions; no unknown mass/volume variants or unit conversions.
Return unavailable for unsupported units, objectives or unsatisfiable constraints within the generation limit.
difficultyDimensions: Magnitude of the exact mass and volume
Density one versus greater than one

assessment.responseContract: JSON object with exactly value:string and unit:string. Exact signed integer/dot-decimal/fraction grammar; no scientific notation or functions. Use source marking rules.
assessment.checkerStrategy: Parse an exact rational and check value*v=m from the frozen question; check the unit separately. No string-only numeric comparison.
rules: Two required binary criteria: density-value and density-unit, one mark each.
Accept g/cm3 and g/cm³ with surrounding whitespace ignored; recognised wrong units are g, cm3, cm³, g/cm2, g/cm².
For a recognised unit, grade value independently; do not infer method credit.

For an unknown/unsupported unit, leave both value and unit unassessed because interpreting the physical value would require an unsupported conversion. For malformed value with a recognised unit, preserve any known unit result.
Correctness, assistance and scientific explanation evidence remain separate.

cases.reason: Undefined rational; preserve the met unit criterion.
Unit conversion is outside this family; do not call the physically equivalent converted answer simply wrong.
Parseable negative answer fails density-value; density-unit is met.

interactionRequirements: In learn mode show a data-table of v=5..50 by 5 and m=d*v, plus line-graph x=volume (cm³), y=mass (g), slope=d, intercept=0; both derive from exact state.
Learn mode offers select-volume and reset via declared actions. At fixed d update m; changed question givens require a new host instance before assessment. No frame-rate-based physics is needed.
Mock-exam mode shows only givens and the answer form; no table of extra samples, model controls, solution graph or private d field.
Provide accessible table/text, keyboard controls and equivalent voice actions. Verify rows/cells, labels and limits before rendering.
families.transferRequirement: After exploration use an unseen pair where possible, then a separately supported interpretation task. Calculation fluency does not prove causal reasoning, experimental skill or coverage of all science.

requirements.statement: The 80 parameter pairs satisfy the stated physical relationship and scope.
requirements.verification: Exhaust the 80 pairs; independently verify m/v=d, positive volumes, seed repeats and infeasible constraints.

requirements.statement: Units, exact arithmetic and unresolved interpretations have distinct outcomes.
requirements.verification: Run every supplied case, malformed-response fixtures and independent criterion-level expectations.

requirements.statement: The table, graph and controls implement constant density faithfully.
requirements.verification: Check zero intercept, graph/table values, fixed d and changed-instance behaviour; inspect real rendering/accessibility when a host exists.

nonGoals: Real material properties or real experimental observations
Conversions, uncertainty, significant figures and general physics simulation
Autonomous model grading inside module code
deliveryRequirements: Content and dynamic packages with exact source and dependency bindings
Bundled runtime, TypeScript source and reproducible build metadata
Manifest-bound reports with evidence or pending status for every requirement
No learner records, provider credentials, undeclared dependencies or install scripts
Use the supplied science/language design rules; do not invent scene kinds or claim unimplemented host tests passed.
